title: Repaint or Replace Your Fort Bend Kitchen Cabinets?
description: If your cabinet boxes are solid and the layout works, refinishing beats replacement in Fort Bend County. See the honest cost breakdown and the real test.
author: Chris Petkau
imageAlt: Refinished white kitchen cabinets with granite countertops in Richmond, TX, Fort Bend County
content:
If your cabinet boxes are solid wood, plywood, or good MDF and your kitchen layout already works, professional refinishing gets you a like-new kitchen for roughly a quarter to a third of what replacement costs. Replacement only earns its price tag when the boxes themselves are failing or you need to change the layout — not just the color.

I'm Chris, owner of The Proud Paintbrush, and I've walked into hundreds of Fort Bend County kitchens where a homeowner assumed a full gut-and-replace was the only option, and most of the time it isn't. Here's the honest framework we use on every estimate.

How Do I Know If My Cabinets Are Worth Refinishing?

Run what we call the box test. It takes ten minutes and it's the same check we do on every walkthrough.

  • Knock on the boxes. Solid wood and plywood sound solid and feel rigid at the corners. Cheap particleboard sounds hollow and often shows swelling or crumbling at the edges — especially at the base near the floor.
  • Check the hinges and face frames. A little wobble is normal and fixable. Doors that sag badly, frames that have pulled away from the box, or hinges stripped past the point of re-anchoring are a different story.
  • Look under the sink. This is the single most important check. A slow leak swells particleboard and delaminates plywood in ways paint cannot fix. If the cabinet floor under your sink is soft, spongy, or warped, that's a structural problem, not a cosmetic one.

Pass all three and your cabinets are almost certainly a refinishing candidate, no matter how dated the finish looks. Fail any one of them, or want a genuinely different layout, and we'll tell you that too. For a deeper walkthrough of the honest paint-vs-replace math, see our cabinet refinishing in Fort Bend County guide.

What Does Cabinet Refinishing Cost vs. Replacement in Fort Bend?

Here are real numbers, not a teaser. A typical Fort Bend kitchen (around 25 doors and 10 drawers) professionally refinished runs $4,100–$5,000, and a large kitchen with an island or built-ins runs $5,500–$7,500+. Pricing is built per door ($120–$145) and per drawer ($110–$135), with a $650 job minimum — a single bathroom vanity runs $650–$1,200. You can see the full breakdown on our cabinet painting pricing page, or read the Sugar Land cabinet refinishing cost breakdown for a city-specific look at the numbers.

Mid-range cabinet replacement in Fort Bend County, by contrast, typically runs $15,000–$30,000 or more once you add demolition, countertop removal, new hardware, and several weeks with your kitchen out of commission. That's a genuinely bigger project with a bigger price tag, and sometimes it's the right one — but for a kitchen with sound boxes, refinishing delivers most of the transformation homeowners actually want at a fraction of the cost.

When Is Replacing Cabinets Actually the Better Choice?

We'd rather lose a job than talk you into the wrong one, so here's when we say replace, not repaint:

  • Failing particleboard boxes. If the case material itself is crumbling, swollen, or delaminating, no amount of prep and primer fixes that. Paint sits on top of a structural problem, it doesn't solve it.
  • Water or structural damage. Cabinets that have taken on water under the sink, around a dishwasher, or from a roof or plumbing leak often need to come out entirely, not just get resealed.
  • A layout that no longer works. If you're moving the sink, adding an island, opening a wall, or reconfiguring the footprint, you're not choosing between paint and new cabinets — you need new cabinets regardless, because the existing boxes won't fit the new plan.

If any of that describes your kitchen, tell your contractor and your budget straight: replacement is the honest answer, and a good refinisher should be the one telling you so.

Why Do Fort Bend Kitchens Age the Way They Do?

Two things age a Fort Bend kitchen faster than almost anywhere else in the country. Gulf Coast humidity puts wood and finishes through constant expansion and contraction, and years of cooking grease slowly break down factory gloss coatings, leaving that dull, slightly tacky film you can feel on a cabinet door before you even see it.

That combination shows up everywhere in communities like Greatwood, New Territory, First Colony, and Sienna, where many homes built in the late 1990s and 2000s came standard with builder-grade honey-oak or maple cabinetry. The finish is what dates the kitchen — the boxes underneath are usually solid, real wood construction built to last. That's the ideal refinishing candidate: a structurally sound kitchen wearing an outdated finish, across Sugar Land, Missouri City, Richmond, Rosenberg, and every neighborhood between.

What Does a Professional Refinish Include?

A real cabinet refinish is a craftsmanship process, not a quick coat of paint over what's there. Every job includes full degreasing of every surface, detailed sanding and repair of dings and worn edges, a spray-grade bonding primer built to grip slick factory-sealed wood, and a hard-curing cabinet enamel sprayed in thin, even coats for a smooth, furniture-grade finish — not brushed, which leaves visible texture on a surface you touch every day (here's why spraying beats brushing on cabinets). Most homeowners update their hardware at the same time, which does as much for the finished look as the color itself, and prep is genuinely most of the job — we go deeper on why prep matters more than the paint brand.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does refinishing take?

Most Fort Bend kitchens take about three to five days on site, depending on the number of doors and drawers. Your kitchen stays usable through most of the process, and the enamel keeps curing to full hardness for a week or two after we leave.

Can you paint over laminate or thermofoil?

Yes, with the right adhesion primer and prep. These slick, factory-sealed surfaces are exactly where skipped degreasing or bonding primer causes peeling down the road — and why it's worth hiring a specialist.

Will painted cabinets hold up in Houston humidity?

Yes, when done right. A hard-curing, cabinet-grade enamel over a proper bonding primer flexes with the wood movement Gulf Coast humidity causes. Wall paint or a rushed job won't hold up the same way.

Can I change my cabinet color dramatically?

Absolutely. Taking dated honey-oak or golden builder-grade cabinets to a crisp white, soft greige, or a bold navy or green is one of our most common requests, done right with a stain-blocking, grain-managing primer system so the oak's orange undertone doesn't bleed through.

Does refinishing add resale value?

It's one of the highest-return updates a Fort Bend homeowner can make before selling — buyers respond to a bright, updated kitchen, and refinishing gets you there for a fraction of a full remodel's cost and disruption.
